title: Evidence standards for multi-ancestry polygenic prediction.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC lists no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI GEO/SRA/dbGaP links and no Zenodo/Dryad records for the DOI. There were no data files to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: the paper is a review proposing a benchmarking scorecard for multi-ancestry PGS (polygenic scores, genetic risk scores summed over many variants). It does not describe any new dataset.

a1_downloadable.note: This is a review with no deposited data, supplement or accessions (checked via Europe PMC and NCBI links). The individual-level genotype cohorts that such benchmarks need, such as UK Biobank and All of Us, are controlled access and require an application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table. A label such as trait value or PGS accuracy per ancestry would have to be built from cohorts that need an access application.

a3_inputs_present.note: No inputs were released. The paper only reviews them.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable, because there is no data.

a5_enough_rows.note: No dataset, so there is no row count.

a6_fits_laptop.note: No dataset. Biobank-scale genotype data would far exceed a laptop in any case.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: There are no counts to compare.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use people's genetic variants and ancestry to predict how accurately a genetic risk score works in non-European groups.
plain_idea.train_on: Individual genotypes and trait measurements from diverse biobanks. Number of examples: unknown, and none were released with this paper.
plain_idea.predict: Disease or trait values, or risk-score accuracy and calibration (whether predicted risks match observed rates) for each ancestry group. The true answers would come from biobank phenotypes, which are controlled access.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians and genetic-risk-score developers need to know whether scores transfer fairly across ancestries. But this review gives us no data to test that.

ml_idea: None from this paper. A multi-ancestry PGS benchmark would need controlled-access biobank genotypes or GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics from elsewhere, for example the PGS Catalog. That would be a different project.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the paper deposits any data. It does not (confirmed via Europe PMC and NCBI links).

verdict_reason: A1 fails: this is a review article with no deposited data, supplement or accessions. The cohorts it discusses are controlled access.
